summary_or_details: Root (wilt) disease: tolerance is claimed; resistance is not claimed (CPCRI). summary_or_details: Complete submergence tolerance for about 14-17 days, versus 4-5 days for Swarna. Tolerates up to 15-17 days of complete submergence (CRRI table). Survived 14 days of complete submergence. Sub1 locus on chromosome 9 is the main contributor to flood tolerance. Under 2-day submergence, 98% survival versus about 94% for Swarna. After 4 days, damage was 5-9% versus 20-70% for other varieties (Bihar/IRRI data). Yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, with yield equal to Swarna when not submerged.
confirmation_basis: Seednet flash-flood submergence statement; rkb-odisha PDF; CRRI varieties PDF; ResearchGate Odisha evaluation; Nature s41598-023-35251-z; ResearchGate South Asia Sub1 field performance paper.

summary_or_details: CSSRI variety information records sodicity tolerance up to about pH 9.9 and salinity tolerance up to 10.0 dS/m, with suitability for sodic and coastal saline areas (name recorded as CSR 27 on the CSSRI page). In a hydroponic screen at 200 mM NaCl, CSR 27 was one of eight genotypes and showed smaller declines in relative water content and membrane stability than most entries, and it kept a lower Na/K ratio, similar to Pokkali and CSR 10. A marker-assisted study reports that near-isogenic lines in the CSR27 background tolerated salinity up to about EC 10 dS/m at the seedling stage, and CSR 27 was among high-yielding reproductive-stage salt-tolerant genotypes. Reproductive-stage spikelet fertility is supported by the fine-mapped QTL qSSISFH8.1 on chromosome 8. The CSC record describes salt injury as less than that of check varieties, with negligible tip burning.
confirmation_basis: Counted: Seednet official morphological record (pH 9.6-9.9, EC up to 10 dS/m); CSSRI varieties page; ResearchGate 288965462 (CSR 27 hydroponic screen); ResearchGate 361442656 (marker/QTL study).
